page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, supported by 16.0 GB of RAM. This configuration maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, allocating 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU. The instance carries 32 MB of L3 cache, along with supported instruction extensions including AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and FMA. It includes no attached local storage or discrete GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the c2d-highcpu-8 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance via stress-ng, positioning in the top quartile. Multi-core processor performance, Geekbench scores, compile tests, and PassMark suite evaluations land squarely in the average performance tier. Memory bandwidth tests yield moderate results, reaching up to 68.67 GB/sec for uncached large block reads. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performs weaker relative to broader instance classes, illustrating a tradeoff under sustained multi-core decompression pipelines.

The dedicated resource allocation and high single-threaded performance profile make c2d-highcpu-8 cost-effective for compute-dense workloads that do not require expansive memory footprints or local ephemeral disks. Appropriate application targets include software compilation, CI/CD build workers, static web serving, moderate database processing, and small-scale model inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing x86_64 architecture. Configured with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 16.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio suitable for compute-bound tasks. The CPU features 32 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction sets including AVX, AES, VAES, and FMA, while omitting attached local storage and discrete GPUs. Benchmark results highlight strong single-core CPU performance alongside average multi-core CPU, memory bandwidth, and web serving throughput. A slight tradeoff appears in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, which benchmarks in the lower tier. Overall, c2d-highcpu-8 offers a balanced execution environment for CPU-intensive tasks such as software compilation, static web delivery, redis key-value processing, and small-scale model inference where lower memory per vCPU is required.
